title: East Asian economic miracle
summary: Japan's economy grew about ten percent a year from the mid-1950s to the oil shocks of the early 1970s, and more modestly until the early 1990s. High savings funded cheap expansion, a well-educated workforce moved off the farms, and American purchases in the Korean War and a postwar boom in free trade helped. Hong Kong, Singapore, South Korea and Taiwan followed with extraordinary postwar growth, driven, Alwyn Young found, mainly by rising work participation, education and investment rather than unusual productivity gains.

uncertainty.note: Japan's high economic growth period commenced around 1955, followed by the rapid export takeoff of the Four Tigers during the 1960s through the 1990s.
